chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Ayoub ibn Nuh who said:

I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the third that a group of people asked me about the Fitra, and they ask me to carry its price to you; and this man had been sent to you last year, and he asked me to ask you, but I forgot that, and I have sent to you this year on behalf of each head from my dependents, a dirham, based on the value of nine Rats per dirham. So what is your view, may Allah be my ransom for you, regarding that?

So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'The Fitra, questions about it have become numerous, and I dislike everything that leads to publicity. Therefore, cease mentioning it, and collect from those who pay it, and withhold from those who do not pay it.'

key_terms.أَرْطَال: Rats, a traditional unit of weight for food measurement
key_terms.الشُّهْرَة: Publicity or fame, here referring to the notoriety of the specific ruling
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory charity paid at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.الْقِيمَة: The monetary value or equivalent price

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying Zakat al-Fitr in cash according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al--Hasan al-Thani (AS) illustrates the principle of 'satr' (concealment) in Shia jurisprudence, where the Imam discouraged publicizing specific monetary valuations of Zakat al-Fitr to prevent the ritual from becoming a matter of public fame or commercialization. While the obligation to pay remains binding on all dependents, the instruction to 'collect from those who pay and withhold from those who do not' emphasizes the individual's personal responsibility and the Imam's strategic management of religious practice to maintain its spiritual dignity.
